Render a manual, without letting one format bring down the rest

Source: R/building.R
renderManual.Rd

Renders every format the book declares and keeps the site even when another format fails, which a plain bookdown::render_book() call does not.

Usage

renderManual(outputDir = "docs", index = "index.html", ...)

Arguments

outputDir

directory the book is rendered into, i.e. output_dir in _bookdown.yml.

index

file within outputDir that the website must produce.

...

passed to bookdown::render_book(), e.g. output_format.

Value

TRUE if every format rendered, FALSE if one failed and was reported, invisibly. Errors if the site did not render.

Details

bookdown knits once and then writes each declared format in turn, so the website is already on disk by the time a later format is attempted. Letting a failure propagate therefore threw away a book that had rendered: the LandR manual's deploy step was skipped and its published site sat unchanged for 38 days because the PDF could not compile.

A failure is reported instead, as a GitHub Actions warning so it stays visible on the run rather than scrolling past in a log, and the caller carries on to deploy what did render. That is only safe because the site itself is still required: index is removed first, so finding it afterwards means this build produced it, and its absence is an error. Without removing it, a stale copy from a previous local build would satisfy the check.

Declare the fragile formats last in _output.yml. The formats are written in the order declared and a failure stops the ones after it, so with a PDF in the middle a broken PDF also cost the EPUB.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## in build.R, in place of bookdown::render_book(output_format = "all", ...)
renderManual(outputDir = "docs")
} # }
